subject: Standby-region SLA amendment request — multi-region failover RTO/RPO
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: standby-region SLA for critical workloads

Hi Karthik,

We ran an internal risk review for our account and want to confirm Redwood's commitments around multi-region failover for our latency-sensitive endpoints. Specifically:

- Our target RTO for service continuity after a primary-region outage is 15 minutes for read/write APIs used by customer-facing flows.
- RPO should be no more than 30 seconds for transaction metadata that we persist via your managed cache/replication.
- We also need clarity on whether the standby region is kept warm (preloaded model weights, reserved capacity) or cold-started on failover.

Current Redwood baseline SLA language lists general regional redundancy but not these concrete numbers. Can you tell us whether you can commit to 15m/30s with an associated uplift/commitment from our side? If not, what are the technical constraints and a realistic target?

We'd like to get this into our procurement cycle next week. Thanks — appreciate a short, actionable reply.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
SRE Lead, NimbusCloud

--
NimbusCloud Inc.
A: 410 Market St, SF

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: standby-region SLA for critical workloads

Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: we can meet tightened RTO/RPO targets if we agree on a standby-warm configuration + reserved capacity and a modest commitment term. Below I outline constraints and a proposed commercial/operational model.

Quick summary:
- Target: RTO 15m for stateless inference endpoints; RPO 30s for persisted transaction metadata if we enable synchronous cross-region replication for those keys.
- Requirement: Standby region must be configured as warm (preloaded model weights and provisioned reserved capacity). Cold-start failover cannot guarantee 15m in all cases.
- Uplift: ~18% monthly reserved capacity premium above current committed Dedicated baseline (or equivalent hosted reservation for the covered routes).
- Operational: 15-minute canary window and automated rollback policy; routable health checks and runbook for manual failover.

Technical caveats:
1) Model size & quantization: very large models (>25B) can extend model load time; for those we recommend warm standby with pre-attached NVMe snapshot of weights to meet 15m.
2) Consistency: to guarantee RPO 30s we will enable a lightweight synchronous write-ahead replication for metadata keys; this has a small P99 latency impact (~20–40ms) which we can scope per endpoint.
3) Cold region network egress and DNS propagation: to hit 15m we need either a health-based routing policy already active in DNS or a traffic-proxy in front (we can help configure).

I'll loop in Hannah for the infra sizing and Laura for the contractual amendment. If you can share typical QPS and model variants for the critical routes, we can size reserved capacity precisely and lock the uplift number.

Proposed next steps:
- Nimbus to share QPS + model sizes for the 3 critical endpoints by EOD Thu.
- Redwood to deliver a technical runbook and a draft SLA amendment (v1) within 48 hours of receiving QPS data.
- Procurement sync to agree on term and uplift.

Thanks — Karthik

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: standby-region SLA for critical workloads

Karthik / team — technical notes from Infra: we can deliver the 15m RTO + 30s RPO under the following conditions:

- Configuration: Reserved warm standby cluster per critical route (models preloaded, GPU pools reserved).
- Replication: Implement a small synchronous replication window for the transaction metadata shard; we will namespace the keys to minimize perf impact.
- Sizing inputs required: sustained QPS per route, 99th percentile request size (tokens), peak concurrency, model family (e.g., r-infer-13B / r-infer-70B).
- Edge considerations: DNS TTLs must be set to <= 60s or we will add traffic proxy/anycast policy.
- Failure modes and expected recovery timeline: with warm standby and preloaded weights, model process handover and KV warmup should be < 9 minutes; the remainder of the 15m budget covers load-balancer health propagation and traffic shift.

Notes on tradeoffs:
- For very large models (>70B) or models without quantized artifacts, warm-loading from NVMe snapshot could add 5–8 minutes; we can mitigate by shipping pre-warmed containers on standby.
- Synchronous replication increases write tail latency; estimate +25–40ms P99 per write — acceptable for most metadata but we should validate with Nimbus.

I'll draft a brief technical runbook and a capacity estimate once Nimbus shares QPS + model list.

Hannah
Director, Infrastructure Engineering

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: standby-region SLA for critical workloads

Team — quick legal/commercial guidance for the amendment:

- SLA language should be explicit about covered endpoints (list by route IDs) and the configuration ("warm standby with reserved capacity").
- Exclusions: cloud provider-wide outages, customer misconfiguration, deliberate throttling by customer, force majeure.
- Credits: propose a tiered credit schedule tied to mean-time-to-recover measured from detection timestamp to successful traffic cutover. Example: 90–50% credit scale for >15m, >30m respectively.
- Term: 12-month addendum aligned to their reserved capacity billing cycle; cancellation requires 60-day notice.

I'll produce a redline draft SLA amendment (PDF) for Karthik to send to Nimbus once Hannah provides the runbook inputs.

Laura
VP, Legal Operations

Subject: Re: Request: standby-region SLA for critical workloads — proposed amendment v1

Alyssa — thanks for the QPS numbers you shared last week. Attached is Redwood's proposed SLA amendment v1 and a short runbook image that describes the warm-standby failover sequence. Highlights:

- Commitment: RTO target 15 minutes for the three listed critical routes when configured with "Warm Standby" and reserved capacity as specified in Appendix A.
- RPO: 30 seconds for transaction metadata keys that are included in the synchronous replication namespace.
- Uplift: 18% monthly price uplift over the customer's existing Dedicated committed spend for the covered routes (detailed in commercial schedules).
- Credits: Tiered uptime credit schedule tied to measurable detection-to-cutover time; standard exclusions apply (provider outage, customer misconfig, scheduled maintenance).
- Operational: 15min canary window, automated rollback policy, weekly replication health reports during the first 90 days.

Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment-v1.pdf, regional-failover-sequence.png

If Nimbus is comfortable with this language and the uplift, Laura can kick off the redline. Happy to set a 30-minute procurement + infra sync tomorrow to finalize pricing and term.

Next steps for Nimbus: sign-off on Appendix A (capacity numbers) and confirm acceptance of the uplift. Once signed we will schedule a joint runbook workshop and do a failover dry-run within the first 30 days.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.
